articles.title: Bears Beat Jets, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Bagent, Swift, Odunze, Top Players
articles.summary: The short-handed Chicago Bears defeated the New York Jets 23-12 behind a standout performance from running back Kyle Monangai on Sunday at home.
articles.body:
The short-handed Chicago Bears defeated the New York Jets 23-12 behind a standout performance from running back Kyle Monangai on Sunday at home.

Despite being without starting quarterback Caleb Williams, who remains sidelined with a hamstring injury, the Bears entered the matchup as 3.5-point favorites over the Jets, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

Behind a strong defensive performance that held the Jets to just 157 total yards and a solid showing on third down, converting 7-of-15 attempts, the Chicago Bears improved to 3-1 while the Jets fell to 1-3.

After eating up the clock on their opening drive but turning the ball over on downs, Chicago's Monangai ran it in for a touchdown following a 12-play, 57-yard drive to close out the first quarter with a 7-0 lead.

Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick came up with a big interception in the second quarter to get his defense going, marking the team's first in 637 days and setting up the Jets' first score of the day on a field goal.

Chicago added two field goals of its own to enter halftime with a 10-point lead.

The Jets' offensive woes continued out of halftime, adding another field goal while punting twice more as they struggled to get their offense moving downfield.

Chicago's own offensive mistakes allowed the Jets to stay in the game, as D'Andre Swift fumbled the ball away at Chicago's 28-yard line. Monangai made up for it one possession later with his second touchdown of the game.

The Jets found their first touchdown of the game a little too late, coming with 9:16 left in the fourth quarter on a 58-yard bomb from Smith to Isaiah Williams.

Ultimately, they ran out of time after an 18-play drive and an earlier field goal from the Bears helped seal the 23-12 win.

New York will host the Cleveland Browns next Sunday, while the Bears will hit the road to face the Green Bay Packers the same day. Both games are scheduled for a 1 p.m. ET kickoff.

articles.title: NFL Fans React to Jameis Winston's Wild Stat Line as Giants Beat Cardinals
articles.summary: New York Giants fans got the full Jameis Winston experience on Sunday.
articles.body:
New York Giants fans got the full Jameis Winston experience on Sunday.

Winston was making his second start of the season after taking over for the injured Jaxson Dart. He was hoping to put together a strong performance after a rough outing last week, and he had mixed results.

In a 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals, Winston threw for 250 yards and three touchdowns, but he also had a pair of interceptions. The veteran quarterback's up-and-down performance didn't come as much of a surprise to fans.

Winston has been in the NFL for more than a decade now, and those who are familiar with his game are used to seeing him post big numbers while also making a number of mistakes.

On Sunday, the good outweighed the bad, and it led to the Giants' third win of the season. Winston was worlds better than he was last week against the Tennessee Titans, when he threw for just 118 yards in a 12-7 win.

New York fans would prefer fewer turnovers than Winston had Sunday, but he still did enough to get the win.

articles.title: Darius Cooper, Dohnte Meyers & Top Fantasy Waiver-Wire WR Targets After Ja'Marr Chase Injury
articles.summary: Fantasy football enthusiasts and the Cincinnati Bengals were dealt a blow on Sunday, as superstar receiver Ja'Marr Chase was ruled out for the remainder of his team's matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars with a concussion.
articles.body:
Fantasy football enthusiasts and the Cincinnati Bengals were dealt a blow on Sunday, as superstar receiver Ja'Marr Chase was ruled out for the remainder of his team's matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars with a concussion.

If he's unable to suit up in Week 5, it may be time to scour the waiver wire for potential options at wide receiver. Let's review the players who will likely be hot names in the coming week.

Darius Cooper's two touchdowns on Sunday—and his touchdown reception in Week 2—is going to have him on the radar of a lot of fantasy players this week. But there is a lot of important context you'll want to keep him mind.

First, injuries. The Birds were without both DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert on Sunday. While it's unclear when either will be back, both are much higher on the pecking order than Cooper in the passing game when healthy.

Wideouts Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon also are likely to be a more important part of the game plan than Cooper as well, which means you are basically hoping Cooper finds the end zone if you pick him up.

Obviously, without Smith or Goedert available Cooper's value is much higher. But proceed with caution here.

With Chase potentially out of commission for another week and Andrei Iosivas on injured reserve, Cincy may need somebody else to step in the pass game behind Tee Higgins. Meyers is the most likely candidate.

He stepped up on Sunday, catching seven passes for 92 yards while serving as Joe Burrow's No. 2 option out wide, with Higgins and running back Chase Brown led the way.

You probably aren't thrilled about picking up a player you may not have heard of before today. But if you are in a pinch he's worth a shot—it's a safe bet the Bengals will remain a pass-heavy offense.

The Bills' wideout was fantastic on Sunday, catching six passes for 116 yards and a touchdown after being called into a more prominent role following DJ Moore's shoulder injury against the New England Patriots. Coleman's been sporadic this year (and during his career), but Sunday was an indication that he may be ready to take on a bigger role.

Moore's injury status obviously plays a role in how much upside Coleman will have in Week 5. But of all the players listed here, Coleman's talent is the most tantalizing (and having Josh Allen throwing him passes helps).

articles.title: Rams Beat Eagles, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Stafford, Hurts, Saquon, Puka, Top Players
articles.summary: Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams are magicians.
articles.body:
Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams are magicians.

Or the Philadelphia Eagles snatched defeat from the jaws of victory.

Los Angeles overcame a 10-point deficit in the fourth quarter for a dramatic 24-20 victory over the Eagles on Sunday at Lincoln Financial Field. Kyren Williams scored the two fourth-quarter touchdowns for the victors, while the Rams defense didn't allow Jalen Hurts and Co. to score a single point in the second half.

The Rams are 2-2 as a result, while the 2-2 Eagles have lost two in a row after going 0-of-12 on third downs.

The star-studded Rams were on the short list of realistic Super Bowl contenders coming into the season, but it has been a disappointing start for a club that was without both Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald on Sunday.

Still, they had a golden opportunity to pick up a head-to-head win against a fellow NFC contender in the Eagles, who were playing without DeVonta Smith, Lane Johnson, Dallas Goedert and Zack Baun. The health concerns became even more dire when star running back Saquon Barkley suffered a hamstring injury in the first quarter.

Despite the injuries, Philadelphia was the better team in the first half.

Hurts threw two touchdown passes to Darius Cooper with the first one coming on an unbelievable leaping catch and the second one coming in the final seconds before halftime. What's more, the Eagles defense picked off Stafford twice with Cooper DeJean and Andrew Mukuba each notching an interception.

It wasn't all bad news for the Rams, as Puka Nacua made an excellent catch and also scored a rushing touchdown in his return after missing the previous two games, but Philadelphia was in full control in the early going.

Halftime didn't change things for the Rams offense.

Los Angeles punted twice, missed a Harrison Mevis field goal and turned it over on downs on its first four possessions after intermission. Making matters worse was its defense was playing well and keeping it within striking distance, as it even stopped a fourth-down tush push inside Eagles' territory.

Alas, Stafford and Co. were unable to turn it into points as the frustrations mounted.

Yet even with the Rams offense playing as poorly as possible, they still had an opportunity in crunch time with their defense keeping Hurts and the Eagles out of the end zone with another fourth-down stop. This one was inside the Rams' 5-yard line and highlighted the overall offensive ugliness of the entire game.

The ugliness, that is, until the Rams flipped the switch.

Stafford directed a 98-yard touchdown drive and a 79-yard touchdown drive with Williams scoring both times. It was an incredible turnaround and gave a Los Angeles team that needed plenty of momentum a boost heading into a high-profile showdown with the Buffalo Bills.

As for the Eagles, they are trending in the wrong direction as they head to London to face the Jacksonville Jaguars.

articles.title: NFL London: 'Money-grab' or celebration? London series begins amid anger over ticket prices
articles.summary: The NFL kicked off this season's series of London games on Sunday but the build-up was overshadowed by anger from long-term fans over ticket prices.
articles.body:
Once upon a time, tickets for NFL games in London were like gold dust.

All 43 games have been near capacity at Wembley, Twickenham and Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

According to the NFL, its UK fanbase has swelled to 18.6 million, with 4.5 million of those considered 'avid' fans.

So in the build-up to this year's London series, why were thousands of tickets still available for two of the three games?

Next week's clash between the Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham sold out in hours.

But the crowd for Sunday's game at Tottenham between Washington Commanders and Indianapolis Colts only reached 60,907 after ticket prices were slashed, and large sections remain unsold for the Wembley game on 18 October.

The NFL is playing a record nine regular-season games abroad this season but 19 years after the first London game, has the NFL reached a saturation point in the UK?

Tickets to see Indianapolis beat Washington 30-13 on Sunday went on sale in July at £79-£245.

But the NFL then dropped prices twice, in late August and again last week. That meant some fans who paid £185 were sat next to fans who paid £79 a few days ago.

Some tickets were also discounted or free via the Blue Light Card and Tickets For Good platforms.

Matt Cullen has travelled from Cambridge to most of the London games and said there were two main reasons for the slow sales; a price hike and a season-ticket package being scrapped.

"I find the prices now mind-boggling," he added. "It's so far above the rate of inflation that it just feels like a money-grab. It's priced out a lot of long-term fans."

In 2019, tickets ranged from £55 to £125. According to Ticket-Compare, , external UK inflation has since risen by about 32.4% and the cheapest NFL London tickets have risen by 43.9%. The most expensive have seen a 96.5% hike.

Season-ticket packages had been available, guaranteeing seats for each London game with a discount, but they were scrapped after the 2024 season.

"It felt like a kick to the head for a lot of loyal fans who'd supported the games for a long time and spent a lot of money," said Cullen, a former season-ticket holder. "But I do understand the NFL wants to bring new fans in."

Why NFL expansion is a 'double-edged sword'

UK fans have also complained about the quality of recent match-ups in London when compared to those in the new countries where the NFL has expanded.

Australia hosted a divisional clash between the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams last month, while the Baltimore Ravens and Dallas Cowboys played out a thriller in Brazil last week.

"It was an amazing game and we haven't had many of those unfortunately," added Cullen.

The best team coming to London this year is Philadelphia, who have reached two of the past four Super Bowls, and their game next week is a sell-out even though it was the most expensive.

The Jaguars face the Houston Texans in two weeks and Dave, another former season-ticket holder, will travel from Chorley.

"We were all gutted when they took the season tickets away," he admitted. "The way we saw it, we weren't wanted anymore because we didn't spend the money that new fans do on merchandise and we get to the stadium later.

"But it has opened it up for more fans to have the opportunity to attend so it's a double-edged sword."

'One of the greatest events for neutrals'

BBC Sport spoke to dozens of fans at Sunday's game and none of them were aware ticket prices had dropped. None seemed to care either.

American fans know the London games don't provide the same tailgating experience they get back home, but they - and the players - are still fascinated by the eclectic crowd at international games.

Fans still travel from all over the UK, Europe and the US, wearing jerseys of all the NFL teams.

"It's still one of the greatest sporting events that neutrals can go to," said Dave. "I don't think there's any other sport where you'd get tens of thousands watching teams they don't support.

"It was always a celebration of the game. People would go for the love of the sport rather than the two teams that were playing and I think that's still the same."

It sure felt like a Washington home game when they recovered a Colts fumble on just the game's second play.

The crowd produced an even bigger roar when third-choice quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis - replacing the injured Marcus Mariota - made a 47-yard touchdown pass to Treylon Burks in the third quarter.

The Commanders thought they had drawn level when Antonio Williams ran in an 87-yard score, but the touchdown was chalked off for a Washington penalty.

Indianapolis quarterback Daniel Jones then got in to seal their success, with Jonathan Taylor having run in two touchdowns for the Colts.

Biles sprinkles stardust on London opener

It is hard to imagine anyone went home disappointed, no matter what price they paid.

The stands were bathed in sunshine and fans looked like they were having the time of their life as they sang Sweet Caroline and Wonderwall in unison.

Oasis' Noel Gallagher was booed when he appeared on the big screen - no doubt because of his football allegiance to Manchester City - and former Manchester United and England striker Wayne Rooney was also among the crowd, wearing a half-and-half scarf.

Olympian Simone Biles travelled to London to support her husband Jonathan Owens, who is a safety for the Colts, and as long as stars such as those show up at NFL games, international fans will want to be there too.

"There's been a lot of anger from fans on social media about the ticket prices but it's only what they do with last-minute holidays," added Dave.

"Even though some of us fans see it as poor way for the NFL to run it, they've got a full stadium.

"We're just not used to dynamic pricing in the UK. It was the same with Oasis tickets for their reunion. We were outraged at that but we still all went didn't we."

articles.title: Tee Higgins Injury, Latest on Bengals WR's Status and Return Timeline Amid Ja'Marr Chase Concussion
articles.summary: Sunday was not a good day for the Cincinnati Bengals.
articles.body:
Sunday was not a good day for the Cincinnati Bengals.

Not only did the team lose 22-17 against the Jacksonville Jaguars, but Ja'Marr Chase was ruled out after suffering a concussion and Zac Taylor told reporters after the game that Tee Higgins has an adductor injury.

Higgins missed much of the fourth quarter with his injury issue after catching 11 passes for 157 yards in the loss.

Higgins suffered the injury while making a toe-tapping catch alongside the sideline in the fourth quarter. He also left the game on the previous drive with an apparent injury.

The Bengals have now lost two straight games after a promising start to the 2026 season, and injuries to the starring receiver pair is another major concern. The schedule eases the difficulty a bit with a trip to face the Miami Dolphins next week, but the absence of either Chase or Higgins—or worse, both—makes any matchup more daunting.

The Bengals were also without Colbie Young (inactive, knee) and Andrei Iosivas (injured reserve, thumb) on Sunday, leaving them perilously thin at receiver. Dohnte Meyers might be the team's top option in the passing game next week if the Bengals don't get healthier at the position.

As for Higgins, the 27-year-old has been fantastic to start this season, catching 25 passes for 401 yards and a touchdown through four games. Injuries have been an issue for him in the past, however, costing him 12 games in the previous three seasons.

The Bengals will be hoping he doesn't add to that tally following Sunday's adductor issue.

articles.title: Dak Prescott Injury, Latest on Cowboys Star's Hand and Status After Win vs. Texans
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys star quarterback Dak Prescott was seen with his right hand wrapped after Sunday's 34-30 win over the Houston Texans.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys star quarterback Dak Prescott was seen with his right hand wrapped after Sunday's 34-30 win over the Houston Texans.

Prescott went 32-of-45 for 335 yards and a touchdown. He also led the team on a 74-yard drive to win the game in the final minute.

Prescott didn't play in the 2026 preseason as the Cowboys prepared for their second year under head coach Brian Schottenheimer. Joe Milton III saw the bulk of the action and impressed with three touchdown passes and a rushing score in two games.

Despite the Cowboys' inconsistencies in 2025, Prescott was one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL, throwing for 4,552 yards, 30 touchdowns and 10 interceptions. In 2024, he was limited to eight games due to a season-ending hamstring injury, and the 33-year-old was clearly motivated to bounce back in a big way.

However, Dallas failed to turn the corner and missed the playoffs for the second straight year, finishing with a 7-9-1 record in its first season under Schottenheimer.

If Prescott is sidelined at any point, the Cowboys would be forced to turn to backup Sam Howell.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson leaves stadium in walking boot, reportedly day-to-day with ankle injury from Ravens win over Titans
articles.summary: Lamar Jackson left Sunday's game with an ankle injury and was replaced at the start of the second half by backup Tyler Huntley.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson left Sunday's 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans with an ankle injury and was replaced at the start of the second half by backup Tyler Huntley.

Jackson was initially listed as questionable to return with the injury, but he remained sidelined for the rest of the game. The Ravens went scoreless without him after halftime and fended off a Titans rally from a 24-7 halftime deficit.

Ravens coach Jesse Minter told reporters postgame that the team doesn't "know enough about" Jackson's injury to provide a precise diagnosis, but said that the Ravens considered bringing him back into the game. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported after the game that Jackson is considered day-to-day with the injury.

Jackson appeared to sustain the injury on a sack late in the first half. Titans defensive end Jermaine Johnson chased Jackson down from behind for a sack on the final offensive play of the first half. Jackson was able to stand up from the tackle and walk off the field. It wasn't apparent in the moment that he'd sustained an injury.

But slow-motion replay showed that Jackson's left ankle got caught up and twisted under Johnson's body as Johnson sacked him from behind. And Jackson didn't return to the game.

Baltimore led 24-7 when Huntley took over at quarterback, reducing pressure on Baltimore's offense before a stagnant second half forced the Ravens to consider putting Jackson back in the game.

Jackson off to another MVP-like start to the season

With the win, Baltimore joined the Cleveland Browns at 3-1 atop the AFC North. Jackson, of course, is a significant piece of Baltimore's hopes in the division and beyond. He was off to another strong start to his season prior to Sunday's injury.

Jackson entered Sunday's game having completed 69.7% of his passes for 248.3 yards per game with 4 touchdowns and 1 interception. He led the NFL in both yards per attempt (9.8) and yards per completion (14.1). He'd added 124 yards (7.3 ypa) and 1 touchdown on the ground.

Jackson completed 15 of 20 passes for 222 yards and 2 touchdowns in the first half against the Titans.

The Ravens are certainly hoping that Jackson's injury won't linger. Baltimore has upcoming games against the Falcons, Browns, Bengals, Bills and Jaguars.

articles.title: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel called for penalty after yelling at official, which set up easy Bills touchdown before comeback win
articles.summary: Mike Vrabel was hit with an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty in the first half of their matchup with the Bills on Sunday afternoon.
articles.body:
Mike Vrabel helped cost his team a critical touchdown on Sunday afternoon.

The New England Patriots coach lit up an official on the sideline late in the first half of their 29-26 win over the Buffalo Bills. It doesn't appear that Vrabel said much to the official in the moment at Highmark Stadium, though he clearly wasn't happy with the previous call on the field — which was a defensive holding call on Patriots cornerback Marcus Jones.

"That's a f***ing terrible f***ing call," Vrabel was spotted saying to the official.

Referee Bill Vinovich confirmed after the game through a pool report that it was Vrabel's language and the fact that he was out of the box on the sideline that led to the penalty.

"I don't know how you're going to give a warning," Vinovich said, via ESPN Mike Reiss . "It's not something that is going to happen twice. When you use language like that, it's pretty much a given."

Regardless, the penalty completely changed the end of the first half for the Bills. The two penalties set them up with a first-and-goal, and led to a 2-yard touchdown run from Josh Allen three plays later.

Drake Maye was intercepted in the final seconds of the first half, too, which set up a 27-yard field goal for Tyler Bass. That ended up giving the Bills a three-point lead at the break.

Now, the Bills still could have scored had Vrabel not been hit with the penalty. It's not fair to put the blame entirely on him, as Buffalo had already made it into scoring position. The holding call gave the Bills a fresh set of downs at the 11 yard line, too. But Vrabel cut that distance in half with his penalty, which made the score much easier.

The Patriots opened the second half with a long touchdown drive. Drake Maye found Romeo Doubs for a 2-yard score, which put them back in the lead. Bass hit another field goal early in the fourth quarter, this time from 38 yards out, to get the Bills back within one.

After a quick stop Allen hit Keon Coleman for a perfect 34-yard touchdown. The two-point conversion attempt after failed, but it was still enough to lift the Bills to the lead.

That missed two-point conversion, however, cost them. Maye found Efton Chism for a wild 23-yard touchdown after Chism somehow managed to haul the ball in with one hand. That put the Patriots on top by three, after they succeeded in their two-point conversion attempt with just 1:50 left on the clock.

While Allen had a chance to mount a game-winning drive, he thew an interception while looking deep for Joshua Palmer. Craig Woodson came up with the game-sealing pick.

Allen went 23 of 33 for 253 yards with a touchdown and an interception in the loss, which was the Bills' first of the season. James Cook had 75 yards and a score on 12 carries, and Coleman had 116 yards and a touchdown on six catches.

Maye went 21-of-36 passing for 257 yards with three touchdowns and an interception. He was their leading rusher with 56 yards on six carries. Doubs had two touchdowns and 58 yards on six catches.

The Patriots, thanks to the comeback win, now sit at 2-2. In the end, though it certainly wasn't a great moment, Vrabel's penalty didn't end up costing the Patriots the win.

articles.title: 'It's not the energy, it's the execution': Todd Bowles, Bucs running out of excuses as Tampa Bay's nosedive continues at 0-4
articles.summary: There's plenty of blame to go around, from the macro to the micro. But the end result is the same: a concentration of blame centering on Bowles.
articles.body:
Sometimes, the numbers tell the whole story. Tampa Bay is 0-4 this season, every single one of those games a one-possession loss. Dating back to December 2025, Tampa Bay is 1-8, and every single one of those games has been a one-possession contest. Cut another way, Tampa Bay has lost eight of nine games by an average margin of less than four points.

Cut it however you like: Tampa Bay is flailing. This is the NFL, not figure skating; you don't get credit for valiant but imperfect finishes. Blame injuries if you like, blame bad luck, blame the ownership, blame the ghosts that roam the decks of the pirate ship in Raymond James Stadium. The end result is the same: this is a team in freefall, with no landing in sight.

The latest evidence: losing a winnable game Sunday against a similarly reeling Green Bay, 17-14 . The almost-as-hapless Packers certainly gave the Bucs opportunities — Tampa held the ball with four minutes remaining down a field goal — but simply could not close the deal.

"We didn't get it done," head coach Todd Bowles acknowledged after the game. "We've been here a couple weeks now at the end of the ballgames, and we're not finishing. We've got to find a way to finish the game."

They've got to find a lot more than that, starting with the quarterback position. Baker Mayfield is out for at least two more games with a thumb injury, meaning that rookie Jalon Daniels is now under center. In his first NFL start, Daniels went 19-for-27 passing for 148 yards, with one clutch touchdown pass to Kenny Gainwell against two interceptions.

It wasn't a terrible performance, all things considered, but when the rest of the team is so ineffective, particularly the offensive line, a quarterback has to be much more than "not terrible" — and that's asking a whole lot of a guy just four weeks into his NFL career.

To his credit, Bowles didn't fall back on the tired "we know what kind of team we are" trope that losing teams use to convince the media (or themselves) that they're better than what their record shows. Tampa Bay and Green Bay had fairly equal numbers across the board, from total yardage (275 to 283) to turnovers (2 apiece) to time of possession (30:10 to 29:50), and yet the Bucs couldn't make the necessary plays in crunch time.

"We can't keep getting close and not winning. That's not good enough," Bowles said. "Our record says what we are. We're 0-4, and until we acknowledge that, and we correct our own mistakes, it's going to keep happening."

The real issue, Bowles suggested, is something more straightforward: it doesn't matter if a team believes in itself if it can't do the damn job. "It's not the energy," he said, "it's the execution."

There's plenty of blame to go around, from the macro (the front office didn't have a backup plan more seasoned than Daniels?) to the micro (was Tampa Bay trying to set a record for most unblocked edge rushers allowed into the backfield to blow up Daniels?). But the end result is the same: a concentration of blame centering on Bowles.

"I can do more. I can always do more. I'll always take the blame on that," Bowles said. "We're going to fight, and we're going to stick together, and we're going to figure this thing out. And I'll lead them to that."

The odds are not in Tampa Bay's favor. In NFL history, only one team has started 0-4 and reached the playoffs: the 1992 San Diego Chargers, who won 11 of their next 12 to reach the postseason. With Chicago, Detroit, Baltimore and the Los Angeles Rams still on the slate, that seems like an unlikely outcome for Tampa Bay, to put it mildly.

If Bowles has any kind of job armor, it's the fact that the Glazer ownership group hasn't ever fired a coach midseason. But he's certainly putting that stance to the test. Since taking over Tampa Bay in 2022, Bowles' teams have won 10 games just once, going 1-3 in the playoffs over that span. And Tampa Bay plays in the woeful NFC South, a division so misbegotten that an 8-9 team reached the playoffs last postseason (and it wasn't the 8-9 Bucs).

Tampa Bay now has no margin for error. Mayfield will be out at least another two games, and the Bucs are right back in action Thursday night in Dallas (2-2).

"We've got to concentrate on us," Bowles said. "No matter how dark the days are, we've got to focus on us. And those guys are real good at that."

Focus is fine. Results are better. And so far this season, the Bucs clearly aren't real good at results. Unless and until they can finish, it's going to be a long season for Tampa Bay fans, and potentially a short one for Bowles.

articles.title: Mike Vrabel's 'F--king Terrible Call' Remark Led to Patriots Penalty vs. Bills, NFL Ref Says
articles.summary: NFL referee Bill Vinovich told reporters that New England Patriots' head coach Mike Vrabel was flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct during Sunday's 29-26 win over the New England Patriots for telling an official he made a "f--king terrible call."
articles.body:
NFL referee Bill Vinovich told reporters that New England Patriots' head coach Mike Vrabel was flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct during Sunday's 29-26 win over the New England Patriots for telling an official he made a "f--king terrible call."

Vrabel acknowledged using that type of language but said he was surprised it resulted in a flag.

"I told him it was a terrible—I'm not going to say effing—call," he told reporters . "I've said that 87 times since I've been a head coach. It was nothing derogatory. You'd have to ask him. I think he was a little sensitive."

Vrabel said that assistant coach John Streicher told him over the headset that a defensive holding penalty that gave the Bills a first down was a poor call but said he could have worded his complaint differently.

"I probably shouldn't have swore, but I can tell you in my history of being on the sidelines as a head coach, I've said that. And I apologized to him," he noted. "It was unfortunate and I have to be better in those moments."

articles.title: Chiefs WR Rashee Rice leaves early vs. Raiders after pulling up awkwardly with hamstring injury
articles.summary: Rashee Rice left Sunday's contest in Las Vegas in the opening quarter after the awkward injury.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs lost wide receiver Rashee Rice early on Sunday afternoon.

Rice pulled up awkwardly with an apparent hamstring injury in the first quarter of KC's matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders.

He caught a short pass on the Chiefs' second drive of the day at Allegiant Stadium and made a move up the right side. Suddenly, Rice stumbled and changed course for the sideline early. He awkwardly started hopping and reached back for the back of his left leg, clearly in significant discomfort.

Further specifics on Rice's injury are not yet known. The team initially called him questionable to return with the hamstring injury, but downgraded him to doubtful to start the second half. He hung around on the sidelines for a little while before finally going back to the locker room.

The catch was Rice's only one of the day, though it was negated by an offsides penalty. He entered Sunday with 190 receiving yards and one touchdown this season, his fourth with the team.

Despite losing Rice, the Chiefs finished the drive with a 2-yard touchdown pass from Patrick Mahomes to Tyquan Thornton. That tied the game up at 7-7 after Kirk Cousins found Ian Thomas for a 27-yard score on the Raiders' first drive of the game. The Raiders entered the locker room with a three-point lead at halftime after hitting a pair of field goals in the second quarter.

Las Vegas is attempting to start 4-0 for the first time since 2002.

This post will be updated with more information shortly.

articles.title: Report Card Grades for Bills' NFL Week 4 Game vs. Patriots
articles.summary: Entering Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season, the Buffalo Bills were 3-0 despite playing with fire on a weekly basis.
articles.body:
Entering Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season, the Buffalo Bills were 3-0 despite playing with fire on a weekly basis.

On Sunday, they got burned by the division-rival New England Patriots in a 29-26 defeat.

Here are my grades for all of the key players from the home loss.

It didn't help that Allen once again lost top receiver DJ Moore to a shoulder injury, or that his pass protection had its share of problems. I also wonder how far from 100 percent Allen might be, as he sure seemed uncharacteristically hesitant to take off with his legs for the second consecutive Sunday.

Regardless, it was a mediocre performance for the franchise quarterback, who made a horrendous decision on a game-sealing interception. That throw was unsmart and unnecessary when Allen didn't need to be desperate yet, and it wasn't his only questionable decision.

It was also one of the least effective rushing performances of Allen's career, as he gained just four yards on five attempts (only his third game with a yards-per-attempt average below 1.0 in nine years).

It was an outing to forget for a quarterback on a Hall of Fame track.

The Pro Bowl back averaged 6.4 yards per carry in Week 2, 6.4 yards per carry in Week 3, and 6.3 yards per carry in Week 4.

The difference is that while he ran the ball a combined 45 times in the last two outings, Cook carried it just 12 times with Buffalo trailing for much of the day against New England.

Still, it's a shame they didn't ride him more—especially considering that he rushed for 57 yards on his last five carries.

Cook also had several key blocks, including a tremendous play in which he saved Allen from getting trucked on a 51-yard Khalil Shakir catch-and-run that went down as Buffalo's biggest play of the game.

The veteran wasn't fully healthy coming into this game and exited after potentially aggravating a shoulder injury in the second quarter. He had just a single catch for 11 yards and played 23 snaps.

This might have been the best game of Coleman's career to date. He stepped up in a big way with six catches for 116 yards, but it was quality as much as quantity.

Coleman made an incredible grab off a deflection on third down during a fourth-quarter scoring drive and later caught back-to-back passes for a combined 58 yards—the second of which was the go-ahead touchdown with less than five minutes remaining.

The guy has found a groove in his third season.

Seven catches on eight targets for 82 yards is a pretty stat line, but he fumbled late in the second quarter and had a bad drop that forced Buffalo to punt late in the third quarter. With Moore down, they needed more from him.

Palmer's workload increased with Moore out, but he failed to contribute beyond a three-yard catch on four targets. He dropped an easy deep pass from Allen on a third-down play in the second quarter, enabling the Patriots to decline a Dion Dawkins penalty and force Buffalo off the field.

I do wonder if we'll see intriguing rookie Skyler Bell get a shot soon.

Where was he? Kincaid was targeted only twice and made just a single seven-yard grab late in the game. One of the hottest players in the league from the first two weeks of the season has just three catches in his last two games.

Knox caught both of the short passes thrown his way, one of which required maximum toughness as he was hammered by Christian Elliss. He was also once again a big factor as a blocker, twice powering critical Allen sneaks.

Yikes. The five-time Pro Bowler was responsible for another sack, was beaten badly on what should have been a safety when Allen got away with intentional grounding in the end zone, and committed two more penalties (one of which was declined only because Palmer dropped a gimme deep ball). He's having a poor season at the age of 32.

At least he avoided penalties this week. And while Anderson again struggled overall with his pass blocking, he wasn't the weakest link this time. The left side of the line is a problem right now, but that's more on Dawkins than Anderson.

Up-and-down day for McGovern. I'm not holding that weird offside penalty against him, but he was beaten badly on a play that resulted in Allen taking a hit to the throwing hand in the third quarter. He and Anderson opened up several big holes for Cook.

No glaring mistakes in pass protection and stout blocking when the offense ran in that direction. It was a solid performance.

I actually really liked what Chubb did in run defense. The veteran also had a key third-down pressure to get the offense the ball back late in the first half and got his hands on Drake Maye several times. You get the feeling the sacks will come.

The two-sack-per-game streak came to an end, but I counted eight quarterback pressures and at least four hits on Maye from the disruptive Rousseau. He was also tremendous against the run, and he did have a strip-sack that was overturned but still should have been ruled intentional grounding.

The rising star actually looked a little off for most of the day and was victimized on several run plays and Maye scrambles. His tackling can be hit-or-miss. Still, Walker spearheaded a huge stop on Rhamondre Stevenson near the line of scrimmage leading to a New England punt late in the third quarter.

Just 28 snaps from the former top-10 pick. He was still being eased back from a hip injury and now has a knee injury. Oliver was technically credited with a strip-sack, but Landon Jackson made that play happen.

Beyond that aforementioned pressure leading to a turnover, Jackson had another strong performance in run defense but did miss some action with a knee injury. He is also still good for a couple of poor angles per game.

You didn't hear Carter's name much across 45 snaps, but he did have several good run stuffs and took down Maye near the line of scrimmage on two scrambles.

I didn't note any negative plays for the veteran, who saw an uptick in action with the mounting injuries up front and held his own. He was quick to recover that Maye fumble in the second quarter.

Last week, I wrote that Bernard is nowhere to be found far too often. That was again the case on Sunday.

He was part of a few impressive stops against the run but was also exposed again in pass coverage inside the box and let both Maye and Stevenson slip away on plays that he should have made. This linebacker corps is not the main problem but isn't doing much to help.

With Christian Benford out, Hairston was utterly exposed in a rough outing against a limping offense that had no business moving the ball the way it did.

The second-year first-round pick was routinely beaten in coverage, including twice by Romeo Doubs on fourth-down plays (one of which he played inexcusably far off the line of scrimmage inside the red zone).

The rookie second-round pick's first start contained some mistakes but could have been a lot worse. His coverage was solid on a wild one-handed Efton Chism touchdown grab, and it was encouraging to see him avoid pass interference on a late-first-half Hail Mary. On the other hand, he was beaten deep by Mack Hollins while also committing a pass interference penalty on a third-quarter New England touchdown drive.

And while he's not paid for his tackling and run defense, he actually did excel in those areas.

It's a shame Alford played just 24 snaps before leaving the game with an ankle injury, because prior to that he had put together his best performance of the season. Beyond a second-quarter interception, his coverage and tackling were solid.

No big plays but also no major gaffes from the veteran, who was the hero a week ago but was mainly anonymous on Sunday.

Several notably poor angles and missed tackle attempts plagued Bishop, who looked lost in run defense and struggled to close in zone coverage. He's out of place too often.

It was a real buzzkill when Bass followed up Buffalo's first touchdown by leaving the kickoff short of the landing zone, giving New England the ball on the 40-yard line. He did nail his two field-goal attempts and converted both of his PATs.

The rookie punted four times. Two were strong (downed at or inside the 10), one was subpar, and one was average.

There were no home runs but also no mistakes. His 16-yard punt return in the final minute of the second quarter increased the offense's chances of pulling off a late-half score.

articles.title: Rams Avoid Calamity But Look Far From Juggernaut One Month In
articles.summary: They’re 2-2 after rallying to beat the Eagles.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA — The season began for the Rams amid talk of a perfectly crafted roster , Super Bowl expectations, and at least one forecast of an unblemished record to accompany their supposedly inevitable celebration under falling confetti on their home field in February.

Things have played out thus far in decidedly less idyllic fashion.

They've been hit by key injuries, ill-conceived travel plans , a debatable pass interference call, and uneven results. Their record easily could have dropped to 1—3 on this gray, rainy Sunday at Lincoln Financial Field.

Instead, the Rams regrouped in the fourth quarter and—perhaps with some assistance from the Eagles—emerged with a highly improbable 24–20 win to keep their season from unraveling.

"Man, you know, there were so many things that we can clean up," Rams coach Sean McVay said. "But for our group to come alive when they did and find a way to make the plays and so many different guys—really proud of 'em."

According to Next Gen Stats , the Rams' win probability was as low as 3.2% with just more than eight minutes remaining. Just as McVay stepped into the media interview room before addressing reporters in his postgame news conference, he said: "You've got to be shitting me."

The Eagles, with a 20–10 lead, passed up a field goal and failed on a fourth-down attempt from the L.A. 2-yard line. The Rams followed with a 98-yard touchdown drive, then went 79 yards for a touchdown on their next offensive possession.

"I think the cool thing about our group is we were steady the whole game," Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford said. "Things weren't going our way. … Any way you can shoot yourself in the foot, we were doing it on [the] offensive side of the ball. But we just kept the belief. Our defense … kept us in it, gave us opportunities to stay in that game. And just proud of the resilience of our group."

Maybe the early vulnerabilities of the widely acclaimed Super Bowl favorite will add to the drama of the NFL season and serve to boost interest and perhaps even viewership in a league built on parity and an "any given Sunday" narrative. Perhaps the Rams still will find their groove and end up playing in Super Bowl LXI at SoFi Stadium on Feb. 14.

But for now, all that mattered is they kept themselves from having to dig out of a somewhat deep early-season hole.

"I'm excited to get on this plane and get up out of here," wide receiver Puka Nacua said in the postgame locker room. "Hopefully they've got some Philly cheesesteaks for us."

McVay and Stafford addressed the members of the then-sputtering Rams' offense on the sideline after tight end Tyler Higbee failed to grab a slightly off-target fourth-down pass to stall a drive early in the fourth quarter.

"[McVay] said, 'Make this thing go. … Wipe it and get to the next play,' " Higbee said by his locker afterward. "He's got confidence in us. We've got confidence in each other. … He's the best leader I've ever been around."

When the Rams traded for Myles Garrett in the offseason and welcomed Aaron Donald back from retirement just before the season, their five combined NFL Defensive Player of the Year awards promised to make them one of the most fearsome defensive-line combinations in league history.

They joined a star-laden roster that included Stafford, the reigning league MVP, and Nacua. The Rams also have a foundation of young talent from their wise use of those draft choices they didn't trade, belying their "Fuck Them Picks" reputation.

The Rams gave a dud of a performance in their season-opening loss to the 49ers in Melbourne after choosing to travel to Australia just ahead of the game . They lost to the Broncos in Week 3 in Denver after being victimized by a debatable defensive pass interference call late in the game.

McVay said at a news conference Wednesday the Rams had been told by the NFL that call was wrong. The league's game operations manual says such conversations between the NFL's officiating department and a team are supposed to be confidential . The league reminded all teams of that in a memo Friday. There is no indication, at least for now, that McVay was fined by the NFL, as the manual says is possible for such a violation.

Donald was on the game-day inactive list Sunday because of a back injury. Garrett remains sidelined after undergoing knee surgery following the opener. Nacua played Sunday after missing two games because of hip and groin injuries.

But injuries are part of NFL life. The Eagles had offensive tackles Lane Johnson and Fred Johnson, wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Hollywood Brown, tight end Dallas Goedert, and linebacker Zack Baun on the inactive list Sunday. Star running back Saquon Barkley had two carries, limped off the field with a hamstring injury, and didn't return to the game.

The Rams trailed, 20–10, at halftime after a calamitous end-of-half sequence. Stafford threw an interception to Philadelphia's Cooper DeJean and the Eagles benefited from a defensive pass inference call on the Rams—sound familiar?—to capitalize with a touchdown.

The miseries continued in the third quarter with an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty called on the Rams' bench for an assistant coach impeding an official along the sideline during a play, followed soon after by an offensive pass interference call on Nacua. Even a stop of an Eagles fourth-down tush push didn't immediately turn things around.

"You can't win it until the fourth quarter," McVay said. "And our guys came alive when they did. Lotta gutsy efforts. And I have a headache from hell right now. But I am really proud of this group. I think a lot of teams would have folded in those situations. But our defense kept giving us a reason to believe."

articles.title: Trey McBride takes issue with referee's comments caught on camera after disputed no-call
articles.summary: There were no microphones nearby, so what Seeman said is left strictly up to the interpretation of lip readers. But Seeman clearly wasn't telling McBride to...
articles.body:
NFL line judge Jeff Seeman had some choice words for Arizona Cardinals tight Trey McBride Sunday.

CBS cameras caught those words, much to the delight of McBride who laughed and pointed it out as soon as he realized that a camera was pointed at the game official.

There were no microphones nearby, so what Seeman said is left strictly up to the interpretation of lip readers. But Seeman clearly wasn't telling McBride to have a nice day.

The interaction took place after game officials declined to call pass interference on a critical failed third-down pass from Jacoby Brissett to McBride. Giants cornerback Dru Phillips had coverage on the play and made contact with McBride before the ball arrived.

McBride immediately protested the no-call to Seeman, who was standing next to the play. McBride's protests were to no avail and eventually drew the response seen above.

The Cardinals trailed 27-24 at the time of the incompletion and punted on the next play with 4:53 remaining in regulation. The Giants won the game 36-24.

McBride didn't address Seeman's comments with reporters postgame. The subject did not come up in the postgame pool report. But in a league where players get fined for their words directed at game officials, this incident will surely be a topic of conversation.

articles.title: NFL Week 4 Winners and Losers: Rams struggle but get a win over Eagles, who might be in trouble
articles.summary: The Rams mounted a big comeback to avoid another disappointing loss.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams aren't the Super Bowl juggernaut everyone expected.

At least they got a big comeback win on Sunday that might lead to some positive momentum. The Philadelphia Eagles, meanwhile, are backsliding.

The Rams looked done when they trailed by 10 points in the fourth quarter. Nothing had been going right. The offense was plagued by miscues, including a couple of interceptions and mostly lackluster play by Matthew Stafford for three-and-a-half quarters. But the Eagles couldn't put them away.

Philadelphia went 0-for-12 on third downs, and they couldn't keep a drive alive in the final minutes to keep the Rams off the field. The Rams stormed back for two touchdowns in the final four minutes to win 24-20. Both teams are 2-2 and neither can be too happy with its start. However, there's a clearer path out of an early-season slump for the Rams. The Eagles haven't looked great yet this season, and injuries are piling up.

The Eagles were without receiver DeVonta Smith and tight end Dallas Goedert going into Sunday's game, and then it got worse. Saquon Barkley came up limping near the end of a run and later reached for his hamstring. He went to the locker room. Philadelphia was down its top three skill-position players. That could be the case for a while. The offense has been mostly mediocre with Barkley and it really might get bad without him, if he has to miss more games.

And the Rams still couldn't do much for most of the game, particularly against a Philadelphia defense that was shredded by Case Keenum and the Bears in Week 3. Eagles receiver Darius Cooper, who couldn't have been in many fantasy lineups, caught two touchdowns including one where he took an interception away from the defender in the end zone . The Rams' offense was poor, and gave away points due to Stafford's interceptions. One bad interception on a needlessly risky throw downfield late in the half allowed the Eagles to get Cooper in the end zone for the second time, with three seconds left before halftime.

Stafford wasn't good in the opener. He threw two costly interceptions including a pick 6 last week. He threw two more picks Sunday. it wasn't just the interceptions. He missed Davante Adams deep after Adams got wide open. He threw a bad pass well behind Tyler Higbee on a fourth-and-8 in the fourth quarter. The Higbee misfire came after the Rams stopped a fourth-and-1 tush push in Eagles territory. Even that didn't spark the offense at the time.

But the Rams' lethargy wasn't enough for the Eagles.

Stafford came alive when it counted most, leading a pair of clutch drives late in the fourth quarter that both ended with Kyren Williams touchdowns. The Eagles' offense was bad without its stars, with just 172 yards. Jalen Hurts was particularly ineffective, which was the case in last week's loss to the Bears as well. Philadelphia has won two games this season but hasn't looked great yet. It needed to stop a 2-point conversion to beat 1-3 Washington at home, and a touchdown with nine seconds left to beat 0-4 Tennessee. The blowout loss to the Bears and the blown lead to the Rams make the first two wins look even more empty.

The Eagles are in bad shape, with a sputtering offense and a defense that ended up allowing 415 yards and blowing a 10-point lead. The Rams aren't much better yet. They have not looked like a Super Bowl favorite. But they got the win, which makes it more palatable as they fix their issues. The Eagles, on a two-game losing streak, don't have that luxury. It's only four games into the season but Philadelphia already should be worried. Hurts hasn't played well since winning Super Bowl MVP and he's unlikely to carry the offense without stars. Nick Sirianni was the toast of Philadelphia after coaching a Super Bowl champion, but now he might be back on the hot seat after a disappointing 2025 season and an even less inspiring start to this season.

Here are the rest of the winners and losers from Week 4 of the NFL season:

Efton Chism III: Of all the possible stories to develop Sunday, Chism saving the New England Patriots' chances of winning the AFC East was far off the radar.

Chism, an undrafted player last year with five career catches for 74 yards before Sunday, made one of the catches of the year to help the Patriots to a huge 29-26 win over the Buffalo Bills.

Drake Maye threw deep to Chism with the Patriots trailing 26-21 late and Chism made a phenomenal one-handed catch in the end zone for a 23-yard touchdown with 1:50 to go.

New England then picked off Josh Allen and got a first down after that to seal the win.

The Patriots would have been 1-3 with a loss and far behind the 4-0 Bills. Instead, New England is 2-2 and only a game back in the division of the Bills, who are 3-1. Nobody expected Chism to be the hero in keeping the Patriots' AFC East hopes alive.

CeeDee Lamb: The Dallas Cowboys needed a win to avoid starting 1-3, and they got a massive game from one of their superstars to lead the way.

Lamb was unstoppable in a 34-30 win over the Houston Texans, who fell to a very disappointing 0-4. Lamb had 17 catches for 189 yards and what ended up being the game-winning touchdown with 40 seconds left.

The Cowboys haven't been great to start the season, and their defense again showed some holes. But they're 2-2 and tied with the Eagles for second place in the NFC East, thanks mostly to Lamb and Dak Prescott coming through on Sunday.

Zay Flowers: If Flowers stays healthy, the Baltimore Ravens have a receiver who can help carry their offense.

Flowers was off to a blazing hot start in the opener with five catches for 150 yards and a touchdown when he hurt his hamstring late in the second quarter against the Colts. He missed a game, was limited in Week 3 but looked healthy Sunday. For the second time this season he had 100 yards before halftime, putting up 119 yards and a touchdown in the first half against the Tennessee Titans.

The Ravens had to play the second half without Lamar Jackson, who suffered an ankle injury , but it didn't matter because they had built a 24-7 halftime lead in part because of Flowers' big plays. The Ravens went on to win 24-18.

Jackson and Derrick Henry are future Hall of Famers. Flowers has been a very good receiver but hadn't ascended to the top tier of the NFL. He seems to be making that leap this season.

Liam Coen and the Jaguars: Jacksonville is demanding your attention and respect.

The Jaguars are one bad half at the Denver Broncos away from being the talk of the NFL. They improved to 3-1 with an impressive 22-17 win at the Cincinnati Bengals. It was a complete victory, with the offense sustaining drives with the running back tandem of Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez Jr., and the defense making the Bengals one-dimensional by completely shutting down their running game. The Bengals rushed for 23 yards on 15 attempts.

The Jaguars came up with a key stop at the end when it needed it, stopping Chase Brown a yard short on a fourth-and-10 pass at the 12-yard line in the final minute.

Coen took over as the Jaguars' head coach last season and they're 16-5 in the regular season since then. They've played one bad half of football this season, and the rest of the AFC South looks terrible. Keep an eye on the Jaguars, who are the best team nobody is talking about.

Bears' defense: Forget the story of Ben Johnson winning games with three different starting quarterbacks this season. Tyson Bagent became the third, helping Chicago to a home win over the New York Jets on Sunday.

Bagent played well, completing 25-of-34 passes for 268 yards, and it's impressive the Bears are winning even with Caleb Williams out with a hamstring injury. But the real story in Chicago should be its defense.

That side of the ball was expected to be a problem this season but it has been far from that the past three weeks. Chicago gave up nine pints in a loss to the Vikings in Week 2 and seven points last week when the Bears blew out the Eagles. Then the Bears completely shut down Geno Smith and the Jets in a 23-12 win Sunday . By the time the Bears took a 20-6 lead with 2:26 left in the third quarter, Smith had completed just 5-of-11 passes for 44 yards. New York had only five first downs through three quarters. The Jets had multiple injuries on offense and aren't very good, even when healthy, but it was still an impressive performance from a Chicago defense that had a lot of questions coming into this season.

When Williams comes back, the Bears' offense is going to be even better. He might have a good defense helping him out too.

Vikings' offense: The Minnesota Vikings' best offense this season is watching Will Reichard kick field goals. Really, it has been their only offense.

The Vikings didn't score a touchdown in Week 2, scored only one in Week 3 and didn't score any in Week 4. But for the second time this season the 4-0 Vikings won without a touchdown, as five Reichard field goals led to a 15-10 win over an 0-4 Miami Dolphins team.

Kyler Murray hasn't been great when he has played, which shouldn't be a big surprise because he wasn't great with the Cardinals before he joined the Vikings. The Vikings didn't get in the end zone, and since coming back to the lineup last week after suffering a concussion early in the season opener, Murray hasn't made much happen. He hasn't had Justin Jefferson most of the last two weeks. Jefferson injured his ankle in the first half last week and was inactive Sunday. Still, the offense should look better than it did against a talent-poor Dolphins defense. The game might have turned out differently had a long Miami touchdown to Chris Bell not been called back because Bell had barely stepped out of bounds before he caught the pass, which was an illegal touch penalty.

The Vikings are 4-0 and that's the most important stat. But it will be hard to keep getting wins unless the offense shows up.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers' offense without Baker Mayfield: Jalon Daniels did the best he could do. He shouldn't have been in the spot he was in, starting as an undrafted rookie quarterback in Week 4, but the Buccaneers didn't do any more to fortify the QB position behind Mayfield. Now they're going to pay the price for it.

Daniels was mostly ineffective starting in place of Mayfield , and the Bucs fell to 0-4. Mayfield is expected to miss at least three weeks with a dislocated right thumb. The Packers held on for a 17-14 win . By the time Mayfield is back the case might be closed on hot seat head coach Todd Bowles and others.

The Buccaneers had a shot because the Packers showed little interest in playing well. Green Bay turned it over twice in Tampa territory in the fourth quarter but Daniels couldn't rally a go-ahead or even game-tying drive. He threw incomplete on fourth down in the final two minutes to end it.

Daniels played OK, completing 19-of-27 passes for 148 yards. But he's unlikely to save the Buccaneers' season that is quickly going down the drain.

Jacoby Brissett: He might not have the Arizona Cardinals' starting quarterback job too much longer.

Arizona might have been forced to stick it out with Brissett as long as they were winning, but they took a 36-24 loss to the New York Giants on Sunday to fall to 1-3. The Cardinals had a chance to win it, trialing 36-30, when they drove to the Giants' 4 in the final seconds. But Brissett threw an interception that was returned 98 yards for a touchdown by Deonte Banks with no time on the clock. Brissett threw three interceptions against the Giants.

Rookie third-round draft pick Carson Beck looked good in the Hall of Fame Game to start the preseason. Brissett would have kept him on the bench with good play and more Arizona wins. But once the Cardinals decide there's nothing much more to play for this season, they'll want to get a long look at Beck. Brissett might have sped up that process on Sunday.

Dan Quinn: Washington's head coach is probably on the hot seat, and by the time a decision is made on his future, his bad luck in London will be long forgotten.

The Commanders had a good shot at a win against the Indianapolis Colts. They were up 3-0 and driving on their second possession when Marcus Mariota had his leg pinned underneath him . Jayden Daniels was out (elbow), Mariota was ruled out after that and rookie seventh-round pick Athan Kaliakmanis was in. Kaliakmanis played as well as could be expected but it wasn't great and wasn't enough to win. The Commanders lost 30-13 to a Colts team that wasn't sharp. Daniel Jones struggled most of the game. But Washington was in a bind after Mariota was injured in the first quarter.

Quinn's Commanders are 1-3. They could have won Sunday if Mariota didn't get knocked out of the game early. But when the final record is tallied that probably won't matter. It was just a bad break, when Quinn needs all the luck he can get.

articles.title: Joey Porter Jr. Reacts to Win in Cowboys Debut in IG Photo After Steelers Trade
articles.summary: Joey Porter Jr.'s Dallas Cowboys debut was a success.
articles.body:
Joey Porter Jr.'s Dallas Cowboys debut was a success.

The cornerback, who was traded to Dallas from the Pittsburgh Steelers earlier this week, helped the Cowboys pick up a 34-30 win over the Houston Texans on Sunday.

He celebrated with a message on Instagram afterwards.

Porter played about half of the Cowboys' defensive snaps but did a tremendous job when he was in, allowing no receptions.

Porter is looking to finish the 2026 campaign strong with his new team as he prepares to enter free agency. He was previously engaged in contract talks with the Steelers, but said the process made him feel "disrespected."

"It was a hard process, a lot of ups and downs," Porter told reporters on Thursday. "Definitely felt disrespected. Definitely felt undervalued. But that's old news now. That's how I look at it. I'm on to new beginnings, new chapters."

Porter's newest chapter got off to a good start Sunday, and he'll look to continue helping Dallas win games.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ $5 million Texas Tech donation gave his alma mater a lasting legacy
articles.summary: In 2024, Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes made a major commitment to Texas Tech University, putting $5 million toward the school’s South End Zone and
articles.body: In 2024, Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes made a major commitment to Texas Tech University, putting $5 million toward the school’s South End Zone and Dustin R. Womble Football Center project. The gift was more than a financial contribution for Mahomes. It connected the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback to the university where his football journey began and helped support a long-term effort to improve facilities and opportunities for future Red Raiders.Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes make $5 million Texas Tech donationTexas Tech Athletics announced the Mahomes family’s $5 million pledge on August 22, 2024. The donation supported the South End Zone and Dustin R. Womble Football Center project, part of a wider effort to strengthen the university’s football programme and athletic facilities.The school also chose to recognise Mahomes in a permanent way. A walkthrough area inside the new Womble Football Center was set to carry his name, while the quarterback meeting room and coordinator’s office in the new South End Zone Building were also named after him.That connection carries extra meaning because Mahomes was once a Texas Tech freshman himself. The fundraising campaign began in 2014, when he had only just started his college career.Texas Tech athletics director Kirby Hocutt highlighted how fitting the timing was as the campaign approached its conclusion."When we first launched this campaign, Patrick was only a freshman and now it is fitting that we approach the end of the campaign with a gift of his own," Hocutt said in the announcement.Hocutt also praised Mahomes for continuing to support the university even after becoming one of the NFL's biggest stars.Patrick Mahomes continues to support Texas Tech footballMahomes' contribution reflected a relationship with Texas Tech that has continued well beyond his playing days in Lubbock. The quarterback has remained closely linked to the school as his NFL career has grown, and the $5 million pledge added a significant new chapter to that connection.Texas Tech football coach Joey McGuire also pointed to Mahomes' wider influence on the programme and university."There isn't a greater ambassador for Texas Tech Athletics than Patrick Mahomes. He is arguably the best brand in sports, not only for his success on the field but for what he and his family do off it."McGuire continued by stressing what the donation meant to the programme."Since my hiring here at Texas Tech, it's been evident to me just how much Patrick truly loves this university and football program, and this gift further emphasizes that," McGuire continued. "On behalf of our entire program, we can't thank Patrick and Brittany enough for the impact they are making on our student-athletes and the future of Texas Tech Football."For Mahomes, the donation tied his NFL success back to the place where his college career began. articles.title: Tyquan Thornton Carted off with Gruesome Ankle Injury, Latest on Chiefs WR's Return Timeline
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Tyquan Thornton suffered a dislocated ankle and will have full evaluation on Monday after exiting with a gruesome injury against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Tyquan Thornton suffered a dislocated ankle and will have full evaluation on Monday after exiting with a gruesome injury against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Tyreek makes another cryptic post amid Chiefs rumors

Thornton caught a pass from Patrick Mahomes and was running down the field before a defender rolled up on his ankle. He had to be carted off the field after the play.

The injury came during the best game of Thornton's career. Before exiting, he had a career-high 111 yards and two touchdowns on five receptions. The Chiefs went on to beat the Raiders 30-27 to improve to 4-0 on the year.

Thornton is up to 219 yards and two touchdowns through four games, which puts him on pace for a career season. Of course, he could be looking at a major setback following the injury.

"First off, I'm just praying for him," Patrick Mahomes said of Thornton. "You never want anyone to get injured and you're hoping its better than it looked out there... Hopefully he comes back healthy."

Further testing will give the Chiefs a better idea of how long Thornton will be out, but anyone who saw the damage can assume he's set to miss a bit of time.

Unfortunately for the Chiefs, Thornton wasn't the only receiver who was injured in Sunday's win. Rashee Rice exited in the first quarter with a hamstring injury and was unable to return. The extent of his injury is not yet known.

Rice and Thornton have been among Mahomes' top targets early on this year, so being without one or both of them for an extended period would be a major blow to one of the NFL's top teams through four weeks.

Kansas City will need veteran tight end Travis Kelce to continue his strong start to the season, but he had a bit of a rough game against Las Vegas on Sunday.

Additionally, the Chiefs might have to look for some receiver help externally, depending on the extent of Rice and Thornton's injuries.

articles.title: NFL Investigating After Refs Yelled at Cardinals' Trey McBride, Vikings' Eric Wilson in Viral Videos
articles.summary: The NFL said it is investigating a couple of exchanges between officials and players on Sunday.
articles.body:
The NFL said it is investigating a couple of exchanges between officials and players on Sunday.

The league said that it is looking into an exchange between an official and Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride from Sunday's 36-24 win for the New York Giants, per ESPN's Adam Schefter .

Schefter relayed that the league is also probing an exchange that saw referee Adrian Hill being clearly angry with Eric Wilson after the Minnesota Vikings linebacker inadvertently knocked him over.

Rodgers, McCarthy Explain Heated Exchange

Following the referee's exchange with McBride, the NFLPA's executive director, JC Tretter, publicly called for accountability.

"This kind of behavior from an official towards a player is unacceptable," Tretter said on social media. "Players are consistently held accountable when the roles are reversed. We expect the NFL to hold officials to the same standard."

CBS Sports' Aditi Kinkhabwala noted that McBride was polite when starting the exchange, even using the word "please." She added that the harshest thing McBride said was, "You're ruining the game."

Those two exchanges weren't the only interactions involving an official, however.

New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel was hit with an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty for using some colorful language, a ruling that surprised him.

"I told him it was a terrible—I'm not going to say effing—call," Vrabel told reporters . "I've said that 87 times since I've been a head coach. It was nothing derogatory. You'd have to ask him. I think he was a little sensitive."

The relationship between officials and both players and coaches is always a bit charged. But on Sunday it seemed even more confrontational than usual.

articles.title: 49ers Beat Broncos, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Purdy, CMC, Nix, Top Players
articles.summary: Brock Purdy and the San Francisco 49ers held on for a 24-14 win over Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos on Sunday at home.
articles.body:
Brock Purdy and the San Francisco 49ers held on for a 24-14 win over Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos on Sunday at home.

San Francisco entered Sunday's matchup at 3-0 and as a 2.5-point favorite over the Broncos at home, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

The 49ers outgained the Broncos by 58 yards on the ground, thanks to the efforts of Christian McCaffrey and company, who helped keep San Francisco perfect at 4-0 while Denver dropped to 2-2.

Defense prevailed in the first half, with both teams held to a field goal over 30 minutes.

San Francisco nearly took a three-point lead to close out the second quarter on a 54-yard attempt by Eddy Pineiro that was blocked, as both teams entered the break knotted at three.

The tides shifted for the 49ers in the third quarter after a fumble on a punt return was recovered by safety Siran Neal and turned into the game's first touchdown on a Purdy connection to Deebo Samuel for six.

McCaffrey and the 49ers kept it going in the fourth with a short rushing touchdown to take a 17-6 lead after a Broncos field goal.

Nix found Jaylen Waddle shortly after for six points, adding a tricky two-point conversion to narrow the gap to three points.

It turned into a tit-for-tat battle as each team traded scores down the line, with San Francisco's Kittle getting in on the fun with a 56-yard reception from Purdy to take a 10-point lead.

The 49ers defense held strong, forcing a missed 60-yard field goal attempt to close out the win.

The Broncos will hit the road to face the Los Angeles Chargers next Sunday, with kickoff scheduled for 4:05 p.m. ET, while the 49ers will head north to face the Seattle Seahawks at 4:25 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Updated 2027 NFL Draft Order After Week 4 Results, Who Could Texans & Dolphins Take?
articles.summary: Five teams left Week 4 with an 0-4 record, putting them squarely in the conversation for the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft.
articles.body:
Five teams left Week 4 with an 0-4 record, putting them squarely in the conversation for the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft.

The Houston Texans, Tennessee Titans, Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Miami Dolphins and Los Angeles Chargers currently fill out the top five positions in the draft order.

There's still plenty of time for any of those teams to turn things around, but there's also a realistic chance they are fighting for the best talent in college football come April.

Four of those five teams already have clear plans for their future at quarterback. Miami has the biggest question mark of the quintet because its at the start of a total rebuild.

13. New York Jets (via Indianapolis - 2-2)

The Dolphins have likely had a chance to see Darian Mensah up close at least once early in the college football season.

The Miami Hurricanes quarterback is one of the front-runners for the Heisman Trophy and is in discussion for the No. 1 overall pick.

Mensah threw for 227 yards and a touchdown in Miami's win over the Clemson Tigers on Saturday.

The former Duke and Tulane quarterback has thrown for 1,438 yards and 15 touchdowns over five games. He's also run in two touchdowns.

There's a long way to go between now and April, but at least right now, Mensah is playing some of the best football among the draft-eligible quarterbacks.

The Dolphins could have their choice of the top signal-callers if the same teams remain in contention for the No. 1 overall pick.

Mensah could be intriguing to the Texans, if they move on from C.J. Stroud, or for the Titans if they believe Cam Ward can't develop more under offensive coordinator Brian Daboll.

Other teams may work their way into the quarterback draft conversation as well. The New York Jets and Arizona Cardinals are among the one-win teams that are potentially one result away from climbing into the top five.

Jeremiah Smith continued to make his case to be the No. 1 overall pick on Saturday.

Smith put up his second straight 200-yard performance and found the end zone twice in the Ohio State Buckeyes' win over the Iowa Hawkeyes.

Smith is 177 yards shy of a 1,000-yard season already. He might be able to achieve that feat in his next game at the current pace he's playing at.

The Ohio State wide out has to be near, or at, the top of the draft boards of any team that isn't prioritizing a quarterback in the 2027 draft.

Justin Herbert. C.J. Stroud and Baker Mayfield would love to work with a talent like Smith in addition to their current wide receiver corps.

Smith could be a complete game-changer in Tennessee, if the Titans opt to give Ward another year under center in 2027.

He'd be such a fascinating prospect for the Dolphins to select, but with so many quarterbacks at the top of the draft class, it'll be hard for Miami to pass on a signal-caller to land Smith, unless Malik Willis shows a lot of improvement.
