articles.title: Chiefs Beat Raiders, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Mahomes, Cousins, Kelce, Top Players
articles.summary: Both teams entered 3-0, but one walked out with a loss Sunday at Allegiant Stadium.
articles.body:
Both teams entered 3-0, but one walked out with a loss Sunday at Allegiant Stadium.

The Kansas City Chiefs came out victorious in the AFC West battle, defeating the Las Vegas Raiders 30-27 in Las Vegas to remain perfect at 4-0.

New NFL contenders starting to emerge after Week 4

The back-to-back Super Bowl champions in 2022-23 entered the matchup as 4.5-point favorites over the Raiders after missing the playoffs last season, per FanDuel Sportsbook .

A late fourth-quarter, 13-0 swing in less than two minutes, and a game-sealing interception by Las Vegas led the Chiefs to victory.

Both teams traded touchdowns in the opening quarter, with Las Vegas kicking off the scoring on an Ian Thomas 27-yard reception that was immediately answered by a Chief's Tyquan Thornton grab in the end zone.

Both teams entered the second quarter knotted at seven.

The Raiders scored on both of their possessions in the second quarter with two field goals, one as the clock expired, while the Chiefs added a field goal in the midst. Las Vegas held a narrow three-point lead at halftime.

Both teams were held scoreless in the third quarter, with the Raiders turning the ball over on downs before punting twice, while the Chiefs also punted twice.

The first score of the second half came early in the fourth quarter, with Mahomes finding Thornton for his second touchdown of the game.

The Raiders applied some pressure with a field goal, came up with a big defensive three-and-out stop and notched a second field goal to take a one-point lead with just under five minutes left in the game.

In a matter of minutes, the game completely shifted in favor of the Chiefs, with a Walker touchdown, a fumble recovery on the kickoff and a quick one-play, 22-yard touchdown by Walker once more to take a 30-19 lead.

Just when it looked like the game was sealed, Cousins found Brock Bowers on a 1:16 drive to cut the deficit to three with 1:46 remaining, giving the Raiders a chance at a comeback with a defensive stop.

The Raiders did their job and forced a three-and-out with 1:26 left, giving them a chance to tie it with a field goal or win it with a touchdown.

An 11-play drive ended with 10 seconds left, with Cousins throwing an interception at Kansas City's 37-yard line that was nabbed by Xavier Nwankpa to seal the Chiefs' win.

Kansas City will head into its bye week, while Las Vegas will hit the road to face the New England Patriots next Sunday, with kickoff scheduled for 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Week 5 Waiver Wire Breakout Fantasy Football Pickups from Sunday's Box Scores
articles.summary: For fantasy managers, NFL Week 4 created several new opportunities worth chasing on waivers.
articles.body:
For fantasy managers, NFL Week 4 created several new opportunities worth chasing on waivers.

Some players become waiver-wire candidates for breakout performances or increased playing time. Others step up when someone ahead of them on the depth chart gets injured.

Buffalo Bills wideout Keon Coleman, Cincinnati Bengals tight end Mike Gesicki and Arizona Cardinals running back Tyler Allgeier each land on fantasy managers' radar this week for one of those reasons.

We'll take a closer look at why each of these players is worth a flier this week. None of the three is guaranteed to become a fantasy difference-maker. But that's why they're worth targeting now; the potential payoff is much greater than the investment of a claim.

Points use PPR scoring. Scoring and rostered data via FantasyPros .

Week 4 stats: 6 rec, 116 rec yds, 1 rec TD, 23.6 pts

When Bills wideout DJ Moore exited Sunday's tilt against the New England Patriots with a shoulder injury , Keon Coleman made the most of his opportunity.

The Bills receiver exploded for six catches on seven targets, amassing 116 yards and finding the end zone. Coleman showed the kind of big-play upside that makes fantasy managers sit up and take notice.

Even without Moore, there are a lot of mouths to feed in Buffalo. Still, Coleman became a go-to option for Josh Allen, leading all pass-catchers in targets.

By the end of Sunday's afternoon slate, Coleman was set to finish seventh among all fantasy wideouts in Week 4. With Moore potentially missing time, there's a legitimate path to more volume for Coleman.

Week 4 stats: 3 rec, 40 rec yds, 1 rec TD, 13.0 pts

When Bengals star wideout Ja'Marr Chase left the game against the Jaguars with a concussion, the rest of Cincinnati's passing corps needed to step up for Joe Burrow and the Bengals' high-volume passing offense.

Gesicki took the opportunity and ran with it, bringing in three of five targets for 40 yards and a touchdown. It was the tight end's third touchdown in four games, which should be all fantasy managers need to know to submit a claim for him. This is not a player whose value is dependent on converting in the red zone.

Burrow threw the ball 54 times on Sunday, so if Chase misses time, there's going to be a lot of opportunity for Gesicki.

Week 4 stats: 8 att, 42 rush yds, 1 rush TD, 2 rec, 7 rec yds, 12.9 pts

Jeremiyah Love is clearly the starting running back in Arizona; heading into Week 4, he has received about 81% of the backfield work for the Cardinals.

But Week 4 showed that Tyler Allgeier has value as a handcuff, if not RB2 should Love get injured.

Even with limited touches in Week 4, Allgeier found the end zone and averaged 5.25 yards per carry against the New York Giants. If he's available in your league, he's worth stashing, especially if you roster Love or have room on your bench.

articles.title: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak proclaimed at halftime Las Vegas would beat the Chiefs. He forgot to tell Patrick Mahomes
articles.summary: The Raiders lost to the Chiefs, but it wasn't a familiar story.
articles.body:
Klint Kubiak tried to provide some bravado against Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs that the Las Vegas Raiders desperately need. The Raiders evidently still have a ways to go, even if they're closing the gap.

Kubiak was feeling good at halftime with the Raiders leading by three points, telling CBS' Tracy Wolfson, "We're gonna win the game."

That didn't happen. The Raiders gave the Chiefs everything they could handle, taking a lead deep into the fourth quarter. Kansas City came up with a big drive to take the lead, the Raiders fumbled a kickoff return, and that largely doused their upset hopes. The Chiefs won 30-27 but it was far from easy. The Chiefs-Raiders rivalry has been one-sided for a while, but perhaps that's changing.

"When there's two good teams, that helps the whole thing," Chiefs coach Andy Reid said, via Charles Goldman of A to Z Sports . "That was a battle. That's what this is all about. It's healthy."

The Chiefs are 4-0 and clearly back to being the favorite in the AFC West after a down season. Mahomes is back from a torn ACL and Kansas City still knows what it takes to win close games.

But the Raiders, now 3-1, showed they have made plenty of strides. The outcome against the Chiefs and Mahomes was familiar, but it doesn't seem like the same, old Raiders anymore. Las Vegas just isn't quite to the Chiefs' level yet, even if the Raiders' coach wants that process to be sped up a bit.

"You find out way more about yourself through adversity," Kubiak told the media afterward . "And so, we have some adversity right here."

The Raiders came into the game undefeated and were confident. On a well-designed play, Kirk Cousins started to roll right, stopped and threw back to tight end Ian Thomas for a 27-yard touchdown and a 7-0 lead.

The Chiefs weren't bothered by the Raiders hitting the first big play. They responded right after with a long drive and a Mahomes touchdown pass to Tyquan Thornton.

The Chiefs and Raiders traded field goals in the second quarter, and then Las Vegas rallied to get downfield and got a 48-yard field goal as the half expired. That gave them a 13-10 lead at halftime and Kubiak some confidence, as he told Wolfson the Raiders would win.

Maybe that bravado got the best of Kubiak early in the second half. The Raiders hit a field goal but there was an illegal formation penalty on the Chiefs. Instead of taking the points, the Raiders accepted the penalty and went for it on fourth-and-2. The Chiefs got pressure and forced an incompletion, and the score remained 13-10. The field goal that came off the board would matter later.

"We're going to be aggressive going into the game. I don't regret it," Kubiak said after the game, via Sam Gordon of the Las Vegas Review-Journal. "I regret not getting it."

Eventually the Chiefs would take advantage and take back the lead. They usually do.

Kenneth Walker has been a huge addition for the Chiefs and he made a big play to end the third quarter. Walker got free to the right side and broke a 76-yard run. He was brought down at the 8-yard line and Mahomes hit Thornton for a touchdown two plays later. That gave the Chiefs a 17-13 lead.

The Raiders couldn't land a big blow in the fourth quarter but got a couple of field goals to take a 19-17 lead with 4:53 left. To that point the Raiders had done a great job getting pressure on Mahomes and limiting Walker, aside from his long run. But the Chiefs thrive in situations like being down two points with less than five minutes to go.

They didn't waste much time. Mahomes floated a pass to Thornton, who brought it in for 55 yards. Thornton suffered a gruesome ankle injury on the play , further thinning out the Chiefs' receivers. Thornton had caught two touchdowns and another huge grab that put the Chiefs in field-goal position. Walker scored to give Kansas City the lead back with 3:21 to go. The 2-point conversion was unsuccessful but the Chiefs led 23-19.

Then the Raiders made the one mistake they couldn't afford. On the next kickoff return, Dareke Young had the ball punched out and the Chiefs recovered. Walker scored right after that and a four-point lead was suddenly 11.

The Raiders got a touchdown from Brock Bowers after that but couldn't recover an onside kick.

The Raiders did get a stop but the Chiefs downed a punt at the 1-yard line with 1:16 to go. A pass to Tre Tucker around midfield was dropped, but that wasn't spotted before the Raiders spiked the ball to stop the clock so the reception stood. The Chiefs got pressure on Cousins on the next play and intercepted him to clinch the win.

The Raiders played well enough that it made sense Kubiak felt they were about to win. He's a new head coach and new to the AFC West. Sunday was a lesson on not taking anything for granted against the Chiefs and Mahomes.

articles.title: Tyreek Hill, Top Chiefs FA and Trade Targets After Tyquan Thornton, Rice Injuries Amid NFL Rumors
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs are 4-0, but they might have to look into getting some help on offense after a pair of injuries on Sunday.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs are 4-0, but they might have to look into getting some help on offense after a pair of injuries on Sunday.

Wide receivers Tyquan Thornton (ankle) and Rashee Rice (hamstring) were forced to exit early in Sunday's win over the Las Vegas Raiders. The extent of their injuries is unclear, but the Chiefs could be without them for some time.

Tyreek makes another cryptic post amid Chiefs rumors

If the Chiefs decide to look for a receiver externally, Tyreek Hill, Brian Thomas Jr. and DeAndre Hopkins could be among their top targets.

Hill has not played since last September, when he suffered a gruesome knee injury while playing for the Miami Dolphins. Hill went unsigned this offseason while rehabbing the injury.

Hill has given fans a handful of indications that he's ready to make a comeback, and he made a post on Sunday that suggested he might be available for the Chiefs.

The Athletic's Michael Silver noted that Hill is eyeing a November return, adding that Kansas City is expected to be interested in him.

Even if Hill has recovered from the injury, it's unlikely he'll still have the same speed and explosiveness he had before. Still, he's familiar with the Chiefs' offense since he played alongside Patrick Mahomes for years and could give them some help as they get their top two receivers back on the field.

The Jacksonville Jaguars reportedly turned down offers for Brian Thomas Jr. over the offseason, but they might be willing to revisit some of those trades after the way the season has started.

Through four games, Thomas has recorded just 105 yards and a touchdown on nine receptions. He was the Jags' top target as a rookie in 2024, but hasn't been able to match the success from earlier in his career.

Jacksonville has two solid options in Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers, so it could be in a position to get some assets back for Thomas.

While Hopkins is currently serving as an offensive coach for Georgia Tech, he said in August that he has not yet retired. It's hard to say what would get him to return to the NFL, but the idea of playing for a championship contender would surely excite him.

Like Hill, Hopkins has played with Mahomes before, so it wouldn't be too hard for him to get acclimated.

articles.summary: Might the Kansas City Chiefs consider a reunion with former wideout Tyreek Hill?
articles.body:
Might the Kansas City Chiefs consider a reunion with former wideout Tyreek Hill?

On Sunday, the team saw both Rashee Rice ( hamstring ) and Tyquan Thornton (ankle) leave the game with injuries, and Thornton's was gruesome enough that it might cost him the remainder of the season.

Meanwhile, free agent Tyreek Hill sent out this cryptic post during the team's 30-27 win over the Las Vegas Raiders:

And Mike Silver of The Athletic reported Sunday that a number of Chiefs would be good with bringing Hill back, including quarterback Patrick Mahomes:

ESPN's Nate Taylor reported that Kansas City had interest in signing Hill even before the Rice and Thornton injuries.

Hill, 32, is recovering from a severe knee injury last season that included ACL and LCL tears. He spent his first six seasons in Kansas City and won a Super Bowl with the team, alongside earning Pro Bowl honors six times and first-team All-Pro honors three times.

He spent the past four seasons with the Miami Dolphins but was released in the offseason following Miami's roster purge as the team transitioned away from a number of veterans, including Hill and quarterback Tua Tagovailoa.

Just how much Hill has left in the tank remains to be seen given his age and the severity of his injury. And he wouldn't necessarily be a short-term option for the Chiefs. But if Thornton is indeed done for the season—Andy Reid told reporters after the game it "doesn't look good"—and Rice is facing a long-term hamstring issue, Hill would make sense as a signing whenever he's healthy enough to make his return.

articles.title: D.J. Moore Injury, Latest on Bills WR's Timeline to Return and Fantasy Impact
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills may have avoided a serious injury to one of their top wide receivers on Sunday.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills may have avoided a serious injury to one of their top wide receivers on Sunday.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter , D.J. Moore exited Sunday's game against the New England Patriots because he aggravated his shoulder injury, but the latest ailment isn't expected to be "a long-term issue as of right now."

Moore exited the Bills' Week 2 contest after suffering an AC joint sprain injury, but he was able to battle through the injury in Week 3, recording six receptions for 67 yards in a win over the Los Angeles Chargers.

On Sunday, Moore had just one reception for 11 yards before he was forced to exit. The Bills picked up their first loss of the season, dropping the game to the defending AFC champions 29-26.

Moore has been one of Josh Allen's favorite targets early on this year, recording 178 receiving yards and a touchdown on 12 receptions. The 29-year-old is in his first year with the Bills after spending the last three seasons with the Chicago Bears.

While Moore has been unable to recreate the success of his 2023 campaign over the last two years, he's coming off a productive 2025 campaign that saw him record 682 yards on 50 receptions.

Now in Buffalo, Moore is looking to be the missing piece that helps get the Bills to the Super Bowl.

For fantasy managers of Moore, it would be a good idea to keep him on the roster since it sounds like he's not set to miss too much time. In the meantime, though, adding another Bills receiver like Keon Coleman or Khalil Shakir wouldn't be a bad idea, since someone will have to make up for Moore's absence.

RAIDERS NAME KIRK COUSINS AS WEEK 1 STARTING QUARTERBACK, FERNANDO MENDOZA WILL BEGIN CAREER AS BACKUP So, it wasn't a slip of the tongue. articles.title: From ‘Touchdown Timmy’ to Raiders legend: How Tim Brown’s unlikely Notre Dame journey changed his football life: “There's no future in football for you"
articles.summary: Tim Brown arrived at Notre Dame without seeing football as his future. His parents had a different plan for him: get an education, then come home.
articles.body: Tim Brown arrived at Notre Dame without seeing football as his future. His parents had a different plan for him: get an education, then come home. Brown even fumbled his first kickoff for the Fighting Irish, hardly the start of a Heisman story. For two seasons, he described himself as “just a guy.” That changed when Lou Holtz took over in 1986 and saw something Brown had not fully seen in himself. Within a year, Brown was the Heisman Trophy winner and on his way to becoming one of the greatest Raiders in franchise history.Why did Tim Brown’s parents doubt football could be his future?Brown’s football story started in South Dallas, where he spent much of his childhood playing different sports at a local recreation center. Football became his path later, and even in high school, his mother was not convinced it was worth pursuing.His parents’ message was blunt when he left for Notre Dame.“There's no future in football for you. You go up there and get that education and get on back home.”Brown has recalled that his mother did not want him playing sports at all. At Woodrow Wilson High School in Dallas, he began on the junior varsity team and was also involved with the marching band. His football ability eventually became impossible to ignore.Notre Dame offered him a bigger stage, but the early returns were modest. Brown fumbled the opening kickoff in his first appearance and spent his first two seasons learning what major college football demanded. He was productive, but he was not yet the star people would remember.“So my next two years, I was just a guy,” he said.That mindset matters. Brown was not chasing a guaranteed NFL career. He was playing, staying on track academically and enjoying the experience.How did Lou Holtz change Tim Brown’s Notre Dame career?The turning point came when Holtz replaced Gerry Faust before the 1986 season. Brown already had ability, but Holtz gave him something different: belief.According to Brown, Holtz quickly told him he could win the Heisman Trophy. That was a bold prediction for a player who had not yet become a national name.Brown responded on the field. In 1986, he caught 45 passes for 910 yards and added two kickoff return touchdowns. The following season became his defining campaign. He used his speed as a receiver and returner, produced 1,847 all-purpose yards and won the 1987 Heisman.Brown has credited Holtz repeatedly for putting him in position to reach that level. The coach did not simply give him more opportunities. He helped Brown understand that his talent could carry much further than he had imagined.How did Tim Brown turn that Notre Dame breakthrough into a Raiders legacy?The Heisman changed Brown’s football life, but the NFL made the next chapter much longer.The Los Angeles Raiders selected him sixth overall in the 1988 NFL Draft. Brown stayed with the franchise through its move to Oakland and spent 17 seasons in the league, including his final year with Tampa Bay. He made nine Pro Bowls and finished his Raiders career as the franchise’s all-time leading receiver.His numbers tell only part of the story. Brown retired with 14,934 receiving yards and 1,094 receptions, figures that ranked among the NFL’s best at the time. He was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2015.That makes the beginning of his story even more striking. Brown did not arrive at Notre Dame believing football would define his life. His parents warned him there was no future in it. Then Holtz saw a player capable of far more.The difference was not just talent. His current pace would put him at 2,282 rushing yards, which would top Eric Dickerson's 2,105-yard mark from 1984. articles.summary: Kansas City lost Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton to injuries in Week 4's win over the Raiders, while Hill is recovering from multiple torn ligaments in his l...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs are reportedly working toward a reunion with Tyreek Hill after losing two receivers to injury during their 30-27 win over the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4.

Kansas City has reached out to Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, according to The Athletic's Michael Silver . Following Sunday's win, several Chiefs players — including quarterback Patrick Mahomes — told Silver that they would be in favor of bringing Hill back once he's healthy enough to play.

During Sunday's game versus the Raiders, the Chiefs lost Rashee Rice to a hamstring injury and Tyquan Thornton with a dislocated left ankle . Xavier Worthy has also been struggling with a shoulder injury, though he did play against Las Vegas.

Hill is working his way back from a serious knee injury suffered last year in the Miami Dolphins' fourth game of the season. As he made a catch going out of bounds, Hill planted hard on his left leg as Jets defensive back Malachi Moore wrapped up his right leg.

The veteran receiver was left with his lower leg pointing in the wrong direction. Dolphins athletic trainers had to cut his cleat off before stabilizing his leg. Hill was eventually diagnosed with a dislocated kneecap and multiple torn ligaments in his left knee.

The Dolphins released Hill in February , making him a free agent for the first time in his NFL career. However, no team signed him because of his knee injury, putting his football future in doubt.

In late July, as NFL teams were reporting to training camp, Hill posted a video to social media that showed his progress in running barefoot and making jumps out of his swimming pool.

In the video, Hill also revealed that doctors told him that he might not be able to walk again because of the injury, let alone resume his NFL career. Despite running, he also said that he had "no power in my left leg at all," which was the biggest step he had to take in working his way back.

Hill played six seasons for the Chiefs, who drafted him in the fifth round in 2016. He was named to the Pro Bowl in each of those six seasons, also earning first-team All-Pro honors three times. Altogether, Hill compiled 479 receptions for 6,630 yards and 56 touchdowns in 91 games and helped Kansas City win Super Bowl LIV .

Seeking a contract extension, Hill was traded to the Dolphins for five draft picks before the 2022-23 season. He subsequently signed a four-year, $120 million extension. In his four seasons with Miami, Hill had two 119-catch seasons, led the league with 1,799 receiving yards and 13 touchdowns in 2023, and made two more Pro Bowl and first-team All-Pro squads.

Bryce Young and the Carolina Panthers put on a show Sunday at home, handing Jared Goff and the Detroit Lions an impressive 32-26 loss in front of the home crowd.

The Cardinals were unable to hold onto the ball and run out the clock, giving Detroit the ball back with 2:06 remaining.

A clutch sack from the Panthers paved the way for a fourth down stop from Detroit, as the Panthers' defense came up big once more to close out the win.

Carolina will head into its bye week, while Detroit will hit the road to face the Arizona Cardinals next Sunday, with kickoff scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Los Panthers de Bryce Young ganan a los Lions en el partido de la jornada de la NFL
articles.standfirst: El resultado dejó a Carolina y Detroit con dos triunfos y dos derrotas en cuatro partidos
articles.summary: El resultado dejó a Carolina y Detroit con dos triunfos y dos derrotas en cuatro partidos
articles.body: Los Carolina Panthers derrotaron 26-32 a los Detroit Lions en partido de la semana cuatro de la temporada de la NFL. Bryce Young lució en los controles de Carolina con 329 yardas por envío y dos pases de anotación. En la ofensiva de los Panthers también se destacó la labor de Chuba Hubbard, quien corrió para 122 yardas y dos touchdowns, y de Tetairoa McMillan, con 192 yardas por recepción y dos pases atrapados en la zona pintada. El resultado dejó a Carolina y Detroit con dos triunfos y dos derrotas en cuatro juegos. Los Panthers dominaron el primer cuarto gracias a una anotación por tierra de Chuba Hubbard, que sirvió para tomar ventaja 3-7 luego de que Detroit había tomado ventaja con un gol de campo de 54 yardas de Jake Bates. En el segundo cuarto, Carolina mantuvo el pulso gracias a un envío de anotación de Bryce Young hacia Tetairoa McMillan y a una patada de tres puntos de 47 yardas que conectó Ryan Fitzgerald para alargar la ventaja 13-16. Los Lions enviaron el juego al descanso igualado 16-16 gracias a un par de goles de campo de Jake Bates y a un viaje a las diagonales de Jahmyr Gibbs. En el tercer cuarto Carolina retomó la ventaja con una nueva conexión entre Bryce Young-Tetairoa McMillan que los alejó 16-22, aunque Ryan Fitzgerald falló el punto extra por segunda ocasión en el juego. Detroit recortó en la siguiente ofensiva 19-22 vía un gol de campo de Jake Bates, una reacción que apagó rápido el local con la segunda carrera para anotación del juego de Chuba Hubbard que colocó el marcador 19-29. La ofensiva del equipo del entrenador Dan Campbell siguió sin caminar en el inicio del último periodo, víctima de errores en la ejecución, lo que aprovechó el local para sumar tres puntos más con gol de campo de Ryan Fitzgerald que los distanció 19-32. Jared Goff logró estabilizar su ataque con poco más de tres minutos en el reloj; llevó a sus Lions 67 yardas en 10 jugadas hasta el touchdown por aire con Sam LaPorta que los acercó 26-32, aunque no les alcanzó para más. La semana cuatro de la NFL concluirá este lunes cuando los Atlanta Falcons visiten a los New Orleans Saints. EFE

articles.title: Bryce Young and Tetairoa McMillan connect for 2 TDs to lead Panthers past Lions 32-26
articles.summary: McMillan had 14 catches for a career-high 192 yards against Detroit on Sunday night.
articles.body: Bryce Young completed 29 of 41 passes for 329 yards and two touchdowns to Tetairoa McMillan, who had 14 catches for a career-high 192 yards, and the Carolina Panthers overcame an injury-filled week to beat the Detroit Lions 32-26 on Sunday night. Chuba Hubbard ran 20 times for a season-high 122 yards and two touchdowns as the Panthers (2-2) scored on six straight possessions after punting on their opening drive. With two of his top three wide receivers in Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette out with injuries, Young leaned heavily on McMillan, and the 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year responded in a big way. McMillan had nine catches for 147 yards in the first half, including a 32-yard touchdown. He joined Steve Smith Sr. and Patrick Jeffers as the only Carolina players with at least 10 receptions, 150 yards receiving and two touchdowns in a game and came one reception and 9 yards receiving shy of matching franchise single-game records. Jared Goff threw for 412 yards and a touchdown to Sam LaPorta for Detroit (2-2), and Jahmyr Gibbs added 77 yards from scrimmage and scored his seventh touchdown of the year. Young entered Week 4 leading the league in yards passing, and the No. 1 overall pick in 2023 started by completing his first 11 passes. The Lions were able to overcome McMillan’s big first half and tie the game before the break. Jameson Williams hauled in a 49-yard reception down the middle against an injury-depleted Carolina secondary that lost starting cornerback Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson to injuries last week. That set up Jake Bates’ field goal to make it 16-all. But Detroit’s defense couldn’t get off the field in the second half and Young repeatedly found an open McMillan. Even after the Lions cut the lead to 32-26 with 3:38 left in the game on LaPorta’s TD catch, McMillan made a toe-tapping reception along the right sideline for a first down that kept the clock moving. Still, the Lions had a chance to win the game on their final drive, which started at their own 13 with 2:12 remaining. But Goff couldn’t pick up a first down and Young knelt down twice to end it.

articles.title: Jim Harbaugh Gives Awkward Response When Asked About Mike McDaniel’s Job Security
articles.summary: Jim Harbaugh gave an awkward response to reporters when asked about Mike McDaniel's job security following the Chargers Week 4 loss. The post Jim Harbaugh Gi...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers are struggling. That might be the understatement of the century, but it's a powerful statement. Chargers head coach, Jim Harbaugh, isn't used to losing. But this NFL season has certainly landed him outside of that comfort-zone.

Following a 30-23 loss to the defending Super Bowl champion, Seattle Seahawks in Week 4, the Chargers now sit at 0-4. It's the first time they've gone winless through their first four games since 2017. While the 1992 Chargers are still the only team in NFL history to make the playoffs after losing their first four games, the 2026-27 NFL season doesn't feel quite as promising.

Jim Harbaugh Gives Weird Thoughts on Mike McDaniel's Job

If you ask coach Harbaugh about his team, he continues to provide feelings of hope and positivity. But every once in a while, Harbaugh let's the slightest bit of darkness sneak through the tiniest of cracks. That's exactly what happened during Harbaugh's postgame press conference with reporters after Sunday's loss.

"Is Mike (McDaniel)'s position as offensive coordinator in jeopardy at this point now that you guys are 0-4?" asked one reporter.

"Like our players and we have skilled coaches, and we're going to keep growing that's…," Harbaugh replied but paused mid-response.

"Wait, wait, does…," the reporter interjected.

"No, no, NO, his job is not in jeopardy. He's a skilled coach, and we're going to keep growing," Harbaugh finally responded emphatically.

Harbaugh's Opinion of McDaniel Slowly Changing

Harbaugh has never been afraid to speak his mind. He, and the Harbaugh's generally ooze positivity, no matter the topic. He's always spoken extremely highly of his quarterback, Justin Herbert, and McDaniel as well — since his hiring.

On January 26 of this year, McDaniel officially became the OC of the Chargers. Since then, he's been in charge of the team's offense. Unfortunately though for him, his team has yet to win a game, and has scored more than 16 points in a game only once so far this season.

That, paired with Harbaugh's awkward response on McDaniel's job security, makes one wonder if Harbaugh's tune is slowly changing on his newly appointed OC. His thoughts mere weeks ago were wildly different than what the football-world is hearing today .

During an appearance on the "Rich Eisen Show" on ESPN from September , Harbaugh was asked what it's like working with McDaniel. Harbaugh, as always, peeled back the curtain in only the way he can.

"He's so intelligent. Book smart, football smart, all the smarts, street smarts, uh, you name it. He's just a great guy. He's hilarious, he's funny. The meetings that he has, I've got my pen out, I'm writing things down, because there's like a nugget of gold that comes out of every one of those interactions…I like to listen to this guy talk. This man sure can talk, and I like what he's saying, and he's got the keys to the offense, and we're all behind him," Harbaugh said.

Will McDaniel Survive the Season With Chargers?

During the preseason, Harbaugh spoke glowingly of McDaniel. Following Week 4, Harbaugh awkwardly hesitated when asked about his OC's job security. Is it possible, McDaniel doesn't make it though this entire NFL season?

McDaniel was relieved of his duties as head coach of the Miami Dolphins in early January. At this pace, it's not out of the realm of possibilities he gets fired twice in the same calendar year. The Chargers next opportunity to find their first win of the season comes in Week 5. They'll take on their division rival, Denver Broncos , at home, on Sunday, October 11.

articles.title: ‘Cannot be covered’ – Skip Bayless shouts out Dallas Cowboys star for taking over in huge win
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys secured a huge comeback win against the Houston Texans on Sunday and Skip Bayless has high praise for one of the team’s offensive stars. I...
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys secured a huge comeback win against the Houston Texans on Sunday and Skip Bayless has high praise for one of the team's offensive stars.

It has been an eventful start to the 2026-27 NFL season for the Dallas Cowboys, to say the least. They secured a huge win against the Houston Texans on Sunday to reach a 2-2 record to start the year. It was a crucial victory as Dallas tries to prove they have what it takes to win it all this season.

Trailing 16-6 at the half, the Cowboys posted a whopping 28 points in the second. Even in the final minutes of the game, the Texans had regained a 30-27 lead. However, Dak Prescott linked up with his star receiver CeeDee Lamb, to get the game-winning TD. And Lamb's performance earned him some love from one of sports media's harshest critics.

Skip Bayless showed love to 'unreal' CeeDee Lamb for huge performance against elite Texans secondary

The Houston Texans have a secondary that most media outlets and NFL analysts rank quite highly. Derek Stingley Jr. and Kamari Lassiter are both considered elite, with safety Jalen Pitre also a huge factor. None of this stopped CeeDee, who absolutely went off in the game.

The star receiver delivered a career-best performance against the Texans, catching 17 passes for 189 yards and the game-winning touchdown. He took over after halftime, catching 11 passes for 140 yards in the second half alone to complete Dallas' comeback. This led to a shoutout from Skip Bayless.

"Unreal: CeeDee took this game over. 17 catches for 189 yards. Cannot be covered, even by two of the NFL's best corners," Bayless wrote in all caps on X after the game. As a known fan of the Cowboys, this must have been a joy to watch for the veteran sportscaster.

As is often the case, it is hard to understand exactly what kind of team the Cowboys are. As long as they have CeeDee Lamb, though, everything seems possible. Now it is simply a question of what the defense can become over the course of the season.
